title: A conjugacy-satisfying interval exchange transformation with distinct continuity lengths is symmetric
author: Przemyslaw Berk; Frank Trujillo
work: Ergodic properties of infinite extension of symmetric interval exchange transformations
difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 489-494: a non-degenerate interval exchange transformation that satisfies the conjugacy equation and whose continuity intervals have pairwise distinct lengths is symmetric. The proof (source lines 496-508) is an induction that is not visible in the statement: the continuity intervals are first ordered by decreasing length, so that the longest one is singled out; the reflection identity is proved for that one by comparing the possible discontinuities of the two sides, and the hypothesis that the lengths are pairwise distinct is what makes that comparison conclusive; the identity is then propagated along the decreasing order, after which the reversal of the order by the reflection and by the transformation gives the symmetry of the permutation.
